title: The Afternoon Brief: 13 verified stories from the desk, in brief
dek: A digest edition: the desk's verified and published stories from the last 36 hours, each in a sentence or two, newest first.
author: GoCheckMySports
key_fact: Antonelli started 19th due to an engine-part penalty and won the Italian Grand Prix, the second-deepest grid-to-win comeback in F1 history after John Watson's 22nd-place start in 1983.
bottom_line: Russell's admission that tire degradation cost him the win, combined with Antonelli's flawless tire management after his pit stop, points to how narrow Antonelli's 66-point championship buffer truly is if he can overcome grid penalties and still win rounds outright.
body: Antonelli wins Italian Grand Prix from 19th grid spot, September 6. Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli secured his breakthrough Formula 1 victory at Monza on September 6, starting from 19th on the grid after an engine penalty and climbing to overtake team-mate George Russell with three laps remaining. The 20-year-old Italian's win extends his championship lead to 66 points and marks the second-furthest grid position from which any driver has won a Grand Prix.

Cardinals, Rockies stage silent protest with crooked hats after umpire clash over hat angle. Cardinals and Rockies players wore their hats tilted in silent protest on Saturday night following a Friday confrontation in which home-plate umpire Doug Eddings instructed rookie pitcher Hancel Rincon to straighten his cap, leading to manager Oliver Marmol's ejection. The incident exposed tension over umpire authority to enforce unwritten rules on uniform details.

Clemson's 51-10 loss to LSU exposes Dabo Swinney's transfer-portal blind spot; historic blowout reignites job-security questions. Clemson lost to LSU 51-10 in Lane Kiffin's debut, marking Dabo Swinney's worst loss at the program. The defeat highlighted Swinney's decision to hire Chad Morris as offensive coordinator and his refusal to pursue transfer quarterbacks, leaving Christopher Vizzina and freshman Tait Reynolds as the only options.

Cubs Hit 200th Home Run of Season; Zeferjahn Records First Save. The Cubs defeated the Marlins 6-5 on September 6, 2026, reaching 200 home runs for the first time this season while reliever Ryan Zeferjahn recorded his first save as a Cub. Michael Conforto hit the milestone 200th home run, his 14th of the year, on a 411-foot drive off Marlins starter Ryan Gusto. The Cubs became the first team in 2026 to reach the 200-homer mark. Zeferjahn, acquired from the Angels, completed 1 2/3 innings in relief, improving on an uneven start after the trade.

Katie Taylor retires as undisputed champion after farewell victory at Croke Park on September 5. Katie Taylor defeated Flora Pili on points at Croke Park in Dublin on September 5, 2026, retiring as an undisputed light-welterweight champion with a 26-1 professional record. The fight drew more than 80,000 fans and prompted tributes from boxers across multiple weight classes.

Michigan 13, Western Michigan 12, September 5: Hail Mary on Restored Second Ends Upset Bid. Bryce Underwood connected with JJ Buchanan on a Hail Mary as time expired to give Michigan a 13-12 victory over Western Michigan on September 5, but officials' decision to restore one second to the clock after reviewing the previous play has drawn immediate scrutiny from media analysts and the MAC commissioner.

Michigan Beats Western Michigan 13-12 on Restored Second, But Clock Sync Explanation Leaves Questions Unanswered. No. 16 Michigan defeated Western Michigan 13-12 on a 47-yard Hail Mary with one second restored to the clock after replay review on September 6, 2026. The NBC broadcast clock showed 0:00 when the ball was initially out of bounds, but the Big Ten's replay system determined one second remained and that a Western Michigan defender made contact while out of bounds.

Red Sox place All-Star Rafaela on 10-day IL on September 6. Boston placed All-Star center fielder Ceddanne Rafaela on the 10-day injured list on September 6 with a right quadriceps strain, retroactive to September 4. He is eligible to return on September 13. Utility player Nate Eaton was recalled to fill the roster spot.

Riley Greene Powers Tigers Past Guardians With Two Home Runs. Riley Greene hit two home runs and drove in four runs across four consecutive plate appearances, leading the Tigers to a 6-0 shutout over the Guardians on September 6, 2026. Greene's performance marked the first two-homer game by a Tiger in Cleveland since Carlos Peña in 2003. Greene, who strained his hamstring on August 11, had returned earlier in the week after the Tigers went 4-14 without him, posting the worst team batting average and OPS in Major League Baseball during that stretch.

US Open Round of 16: Ten Americans Remain, Five Men Mark Strongest Male Contingent Since 1995. Ten American players (five men, five women) reached the round of 16 at the 2026 US Open, part of a total of 15 American singles players advancing to the third round. The tally marks the most American men into the fourth round since 1995 and the most total American third-round advances since 2002.

Vikings re-sign Harrison Smith on 1-year, $12.25 million deal for 15th season. Harrison Smith, released by the Minnesota Vikings in March, re-signed on a one-year deal worth $12.25 million with incentives reaching $16.25 million after the team's replacement, Jamal Adams, tore his knee in the preseason. Defensive coordinator Brian Flores reportedly pushed for Smith's return.

Vikings re-sign Harrison Smith to one-year, $12.25M deal for 15th season. Safety Harrison Smith returns to the Minnesota Vikings for his 15th NFL season on a one-year, $12.25 million contract. The 37-year-old is a six-time Pro Bowler and one-time All-Pro who has spent his entire career with the franchise.

Zheng rallies past Keys, Potapova stuns Anisimova at US Open third round on September 5. Zheng Qinwen rallied from a set down to defeat No. 22 seed Madison Keys 1-6, 7-6 (3), 7-5 on September 5, 2026. In the same round, Anastasia Potapova upset No. 10 seed Amanda Anisimova 6-2, 7-5. Both players reached the fourth round of the US Open with dominant performances in the decisive sets.
